mainTopic: Why a house smaller than four by four אמות is not treated as a real house, and lowering a too-tall סוכה
overview: This amud explains a ברייתא that lists the הלכות that do not apply to a house smaller than four by four אמות. The גמרא first asks whether the ברייתא follows only רבי, who requires four by four for a סוכה. It answers that even the רבנן agree: a סוכה is a temporary home and can be small, but a permanent house must be four by four or no one would live in it. Torah laws such as מזוזה and מעקה do not apply to it, because they say בית and this is not a בית. Rabbinic עירוב rules leave it out because it is not fit to live in, though the food of a שיתוף may still be placed there, since it is no worse than a courtyard. A tiny house also cannot join two cities, because unlike a watchman's hut it does not serve its purpose. It gets no share when a courtyard is divided, because it is expected to be torn down. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה and rules that cushions and blankets on the floor do not lower a סוכה that is taller than twenty אמות.

steps.title: The last two rules of the ברייתא about a tiny house
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its list: a house smaller than four by four אמות cannot link two towns as an עיבור, and brothers or partners cannot divide it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And such a house is not used as an extension linking two towns, and brothers and partners do not divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a ברייתא that lists rules for a house smaller than four by four אמות. These are the last two items on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a house standing between two nearby towns can join them into one town for measuring the תחום שבת. A house this small does not count, so it cannot do that. Also, if two brothers or partners own it, one cannot force a split, because it is too small to divide.

keyTerms.meaning: An extension of a town's border, here a house that links two towns into one for measuring the תחום שבת
Towns
Partners who own something together
Divide, split up shared property

phrases.english: And one does not make it an extension
phrases.notes: "It" is the house smaller than four by four אמות that the ברייתא has been talking about.

phrases.english: between two towns,
and brothers and partners do not divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ עִיבּוּר בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun earlier on the דף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house under four by four אמות does not serve as an עיבור between towns and is not divided between brothers or partners.

steps.title: Does this ברייתא only follow רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא, which treats four by four as the minimum, follows רבי and not the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this ברייתא is רבי's view and not the רבנן's?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ברייתא follows. It suggests that it matches רבי, who requires four by four אמות for a סוכה, and not the רבנן, who allow a smaller סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, רבי said a סוכה must be at least four by four אמות, and the רבנן said it can be smaller. Since this ברייתא also uses four by four as the cutoff for a house, it seems to fit only רבי. If that were true, the ברייתא would stand against the majority view, so the גמרא is setting up the next step to check this.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A suggestion that the גמרא usually goes on to reject
The Sages, here the majority who argue with רבי

steps.confusionAlert: לֵימָא is only a suggestion. The גמרא is not deciding that the ברייתא follows רבי. In the very next step it rejects this idea.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is Rabbi and not the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: This points back to the argument earlier on the דף about the smallest size of a סוכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which תנא the ברייתא just quoted follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא's four by four minimum for a house can only fit רבי's view on סוכה

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree a real house needs four by four
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected. The רבנן allow a small סוכה only because a סוכה is a temporary home. A permanent house must be four by four, or no one would live in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the רבנן. They allow a small size only for a סוכה, because it is a temporary home. But for a house, which is a permanent home, even the רבנן agree: if it has four by four אמות people live in it, and if not, people do not live in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the ברייתא follows only רבי. It explains that the רבנן's lenient size was only for a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is between a temporary home and a permanent one. A person is willing to squeeze into a small space for seven days, so a small סוכה still counts. A permanent house smaller than four by four is not a place people really live, so even the רבנן agree it does not count as a house.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say, used to show that a source also fits the other opinion
They only said their view up to here, which limits an opinion to its own case
A temporary dwelling
A permanent dwelling
They agree, they concede

steps.whatToRemember: A סוכה is a דירת עראי, so it can be small according to the רבנן. A בית is a דירת קבע, so everyone agrees it needs at least four by four אמות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key idea for the rest of the section: whether a space counts as a house depends on whether people would really live in it.

phrases.english: Even if you say it is the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
phrases.english: the Rabbis only said it there
with regard to a sukka,
which is a temporary dwelling,
but with regard to a house,
which is a permanent dwelling,
even the Rabbis agree

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אִית בֵּיהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת —
phrases.english: that if it has four cubits by four cubits,
people live in it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לָא דָּיְירִי בֵּיהּ אִינָשֵׁי.
phrases.english: and if not, people do not live in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא must follow רבי alone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion wrongly assumed the רבנן's lenient size for סוכה also applies to a permanent house

steps.title: Quoting the Torah-based rules from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to quote the first rules of the ברייתא: a tiny house is free from מזוזה and מעקה, does not get צרעת, is not sold permanently like houses in walled cities, and does not send a soldier home from war.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: such a house is exempt from מזוזה and from a fence on the roof. It does not become impure with צרעת of houses. Its sale is not made final like houses in walled cities. And a soldier does not go home from the battle lines because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the ברייתא's list to explain it. Here it quotes the first group of rules, and it is setting up the question of why they apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these rules is a Torah law that is normally tied to a house. The ברייתא says none of them apply to a space smaller than four by four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: The scroll placed on a doorpost
A protective fence around a flat roof
צרעת marks, here the kind that can appear on a house
Becomes permanently final, a sale that cannot be bought back
Houses in walled cities, whose sale becomes final after one year
The battle lines, from which certain soldiers are sent home

phrases.english: The Master said:
It is exempt from mezuza and from a parapet,
and it does not become impure with leprous marks,
and it is not sold permanently as with houses of walled cities,
and one does not return from the battle lines because of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא to explain its rules one by one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house under four by four אמות is exempt from מזוזה and מעקה, is not affected by נגעים, is not subject to the walled-city sale rule, and does not exempt a soldier from war.

steps.title: Reason: the Torah uses the word בית
steps.stepSummary: All these rules apply only to a בית, and a space smaller than four by four is not a בית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the word "house" is written about all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why these rules do not apply to a tiny house, and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each of these laws the Torah uses the word בית. Since step 3 showed that a space under four by four is not a real home, it is not a בית, so none of these laws apply.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
It is written in the Torah
In all of them

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because "house" is written in all of them.
phrases.notes: See דברים 6:9, דברים 22:8, ויקרא 14:34, ויקרא 25:30, and דברים 20:5.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּבַיִת כְּתִיב בְּהוּ בְּכוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the rules quoted in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: These Torah laws all say בית, and a space smaller than four by four אמות does not count as a בית.

steps.title: Quoting the rabbinic עירוב rules from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next group from the ברייתא: a tiny house is not part of עירובי חצירות or a שיתוף, and the עירוב food is not placed in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one does not make an עירוב for it, and one does not make a שיתוף for it, and one does not place the עירוב in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the ברייתא, now the rules about the rabbinic עירוב system. It is setting up the question of why these apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are rabbinic laws, not Torah laws, so the word בית from step 5 cannot be the reason. The residents of a tiny house do not need to join the courtyard's עירוב, and the alleyway's שיתוף does not need to include them.

keyTerms.meaning: Make an עירוב חצירות, joining the houses of a courtyard so carrying is allowed on שבת
Make a שיתוף מבואות, joining the courtyards that open onto an alleyway
The shared food that makes the joining work

phrases.english: And one does not make a joining of courtyards for it,
and one does not make a merging of alleyways for it,
and one does not place the eruv in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין בּוֹ, וְאֵין מִשְׁתַּתְּפִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the Torah-based rules to the rabbinic rules in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house under four by four אמות is left out of עירוב and שיתוף, and the עירוב food is not placed in it.

steps.title: Reason: it is not fit to live in
steps.stepSummary: The rabbinic עירוב rules do not apply because a space this small is not fit for living.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because it is not fit for living in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason for the rabbinic rules. A tiny house is not a real place to live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word בית is not the reason, because these are rabbinic laws. The reason is the idea from step 3: people do not really live in a space under four by four. The עירוב system is about joining people's homes, so a place that is not a home is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, suitable
A dwelling, a place to live

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because it is not fit for dwelling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the rules quoted in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A space under four by four אמות is not fit to live in, so it is not part of the עירוב system.

steps.title: Only עירובי חצירות is ruled out; a שיתוף may be placed there
steps.stepSummary: The ban on placing the עירוב there applies only to עירובי חצירות. The food of a שיתוף may be placed in a tiny house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The food of עירובי חצירות is not placed in it, but the food of a שיתוף is placed in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes clear which עירוב the ברייתא meant when it said one may not place the עירוב in a tiny house. It meant only עירובי חצירות, not a שיתוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason from step 7, that the place is not fit to live in, matters only for עירובי חצירות, whose food must sit in a home. A שיתוף does not need a real dwelling, so it can be left even in a space this small. This shows that the ברייתא's word עירוב was used in a narrow sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The joining of the houses that open onto a courtyard
Short for שיתוף מבואות, the joining of courtyards that open onto an alleyway

steps.whatToRemember: Torah laws that say בית do not apply to a space under four by four אמות, because it is not a בית. The rabbinic עירובי חצירות rules also leave it out, because it is not fit to live in. But a שיתוף may still be placed there.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of joining. עירובי חצירות joins houses in a courtyard, and its food cannot go in the tiny house. שיתוף joins courtyards in an alleyway, and its food can go there.

phrases.english: The joining of courtyards, one does not place in it,
but the merging of alleyways, one places in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵירוּבֵי חֲצֵירוֹת אֵין מַנִּיחִין בּוֹ, אֲבָל שִׁיתּוּף מַנִּיחִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ברייתא's rule about placing the עירוב, based on the reason given in step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A space under four by four אמות cannot hold the food of עירובי חצירות because it is not fit to live in, but the food of a שיתוף may be placed there.

steps.title: Why can a שיתוף be placed in a tiny house?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the distinction it just made in step 8.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the food of a שיתוף may be placed in a tiny house when the food of an עירוב חצירות may not. This short question sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said a tiny house is not fit for living. So it seems strange that it could hold any עירוב food at all. The גמרא wants to know what makes a שיתוף different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why may the שיתוף food go into a tiny house, when the עירוב חצירות food may not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the distinction made in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a tiny house may hold the food of a שיתוף even though it is not fit for living.

steps.title: A tiny house is no worse than a courtyard in the alley
steps.stepSummary: A tiny house is no less a place than a courtyard that opens into the alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is no worse than a courtyard that is in the alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a tiny house is no worse than a courtyard that opens into the alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard has no roof and is not a real home, yet the food of a שיתוף may be placed there. So the food of a שיתוף does not need a real house. A tiny house, which is at least as good as a courtyard, also works.

keyTerms.meaning: It is no worse; it is not on a lower level
A courtyard that opens into the alley

phrases.english: Because it is no worse than a courtyard that is in the alley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The food of a שיתוף may be placed in a courtyard, and a tiny house is no worse than a courtyard.

steps.title: Source: each עירוב goes in its own area
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a source: an עירוב חצירות goes in the courtyard, and a שיתוף goes in the alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: The עירוב חצירות is placed in the courtyard, and the שיתוף of the alley is placed in the alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that the food of a שיתוף may be placed somewhere that is not a real house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source matches each kind of עירוב with a larger area: an עירוב חצירות with the courtyard and a שיתוף with the alley. It is brought to show that a שיתוף can sit in a place like a courtyard. As written, though, it raises a problem, which the גמרא takes up next.

keyTerms.meaning: The shared food that lets the courtyards of an alley carry in the alley on שבת
An alley that several courtyards open into

phrases.english: As we learned: The עירוב חצירות is placed in the courtyard,
and the שיתוף of the alley is placed in the alley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the answer of step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That the food of a שיתוף may be placed in a place that is not a real house, such as a courtyard.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ruling quoted from מסכת עירובין about where each type of עירוב is placed.

steps.title: An עירוב חצירות in a courtyard? Another source says no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that the source was already challenged: a משנה says an עירוב placed in a gatehouse, portico or balcony is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: Is the עירוב חצירות really placed in the courtyard? But we learned: One who places his עירוב in a gatehouse, a portico, or a balcony, it is not an עירוב, and one who lives there does not forbid the others to carry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls a challenge that was raised against this source in מסכת עירובין. If an עירוב placed in a gatehouse or on a balcony does not count, then surely it cannot be placed in an open courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that an עירוב חצירות must be placed in a real house, not in side areas like a gatehouse or balcony. A courtyard is even less of a house than those areas. So the plain words 'עירוב חצירות in the courtyard' cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (a challenge raised earlier on this source)
Gatehouse, a small room at the entrance
Portico, a roofed area without full walls
Balcony
Forbids the others to carry because he did not join the עירוב

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
Is the עירוב חצירות really placed in the courtyard?
But we learned: One who places his עירוב
in a gatehouse, a portico, or a balcony,
it is not an עירוב,
and one who lives there does not forbid the others to carry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ, עֵירוּבֵי חֲצֵירוֹת בֶּחָצֵר? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain wording of the source quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'עירובי חצירות בחצר' in the source of step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עירוב placed in a gatehouse, portico or balcony is not valid because those are not houses. A courtyard is surely no better, so an עירוב חצירות cannot be placed in a courtyard.

steps.title: Corrected reading: a house in the courtyard, a courtyard in the alley
steps.stepSummary: The source is reread: the עירוב חצירות goes in a house in the courtyard, and the שיתוף goes in a courtyard that opens into the alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: The עירוב חצירות is placed in a house that is in the courtyard, and the שיתוף of the alleys is placed in a courtyard that is in the alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the source. An עירוב חצירות must be placed in a real house that opens into the courtyard, while a שיתוף may be placed in a courtyard that opens into the alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The corrected reading fits the משנה, because an עירוב חצירות now sits in a real house. It also shows the key point: the food of a שיתוף may sit in a courtyard, which is not a real home.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (the wording is corrected)
A house that opens into the courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'in the courtyard' and 'in the alley' do not mean out in the open space. Each עירוב goes into one of the smaller units that open into that area: a house for the courtyard, and a courtyard for the alley.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
The עירוב חצירות is placed in a house that is in the courtyard,
and the שיתוף of the alleys is placed in a courtyard that is in the alley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by rereading the source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source seemed to say that an עירוב חצירות may be placed in the open courtyard itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: An עירוב חצירות goes in a house that opens into the courtyard, and a שיתוף may go in a courtyard that opens into the alley.

steps.title: So a tiny house can hold the שיתוף
steps.stepSummary: A tiny house is no worse than a courtyard in the alley, so the food of a שיתוף may be placed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this tiny house is no worse than a courtyard that is in the alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the corrected source to the tiny house. Since the food of a שיתוף may be placed in a courtyard, it may also be placed in a tiny house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the explanation that began in step 9. The proof works only for a שיתוף, because only the שיתוף may be placed in a courtyard. An עירוב חצירות still needs a real house, so it still cannot go in a tiny house.

keyTerms.meaning: And this one (the tiny house)

steps.whatToRemember: An עירוב חצירות must be placed in a real house. The food of a שיתוף may be placed even in a courtyard, so it may also go in a house smaller than four by four.

phrases.english: And this one is no worse than a courtyard that is in the alley.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the tiny house, smaller than four by four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the corrected reading of step 13 to the tiny house.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The food of a שיתוף may be placed in a tiny house, because a tiny house is no worse than a courtyard, where a שיתוף may be placed.

steps.title: A tiny house does not extend a city's boundary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next rule of the ברייתא: a tiny house is not counted as an extension of a city when it stands between two cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one does not make it an extension of the city between two cities.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next rule of the ברייתא. A tiny house standing between two cities does not extend the city's boundary, so it cannot help join the two cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For measuring the תחום שבת, nearby houses can count as part of a city and extend its edge. Normally this can make two close cities count as one. The ברייתא says a tiny house cannot do this.

keyTerms.meaning: An extension of a city's boundary, used when measuring the תחום
The distance one may walk outside a city on שבת
Towns, cities

phrases.english: And one does not make it an extension of the city
between two cities.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ עִיבּוּר בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next rule in the ברייתא, like steps 4 and 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house smaller than four by four does not count as an extension of a city to join it with another city.

steps.title: Not even counted like a watchman's hut
steps.stepSummary: The tiny house is not even counted like the huts of field watchmen.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we do not even treat it like watchmen's huts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the rule: a tiny house is not even treated like a watchman's hut. Huts like these can join two cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A watchman's hut is a flimsy structure, yet it counts for joining two cities. The tiny house does not reach even that low level. This is a strong statement, and it leads to the question of why.

keyTerms.meaning: Huts used by watchmen guarding the fields
We treat it as, we give it the status of

phrases.english: For we do not even treat it like watchmen's huts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the rule of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tiny house is not even treated like a watchman's hut, which does join two cities.

steps.title: Why is it worse than a hut?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a tiny house is worse than a flimsy watchman's hut.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a tiny house should count for less than a weak hut. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny house might seem sturdier than a hut. So it is surprising that the hut counts and the tiny house does not.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why does a flimsy hut count when a tiny house does not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a tiny house is treated as worse than a watchman's hut.

steps.title: Huts fit their purpose; the tiny house does not
steps.stepSummary: Huts are suited to what they are used for, but a tiny house is not suited to its purpose of living.
steps.simpleTranslation: Huts are fit for their purpose, but this one is not fit for its purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a watchman's hut does its job well, but a tiny house does not do its job of being a home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something counts by how well it serves its own purpose, not by how strong it is. A hut only has to shelter a watchman, and it does. A house has to be a place to live, and a house smaller than four by four is not fit for that.

keyTerms.meaning: They are fit for their purpose
It is not fit

steps.whatToRemember: A house smaller than four by four is not fit for living, so it does not join two cities, even though a watchman's hut, which does serve its purpose, does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This repeats the main idea of the whole ברייתא: a space smaller than four by four does not count as a real house.

phrases.english: Huts are fit for their purpose,
but this one is not fit for its purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A watchman's hut serves its purpose, but a tiny house cannot serve its purpose as a home.

steps.title: Brothers and partners do not divide a tiny house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another rule from the ברייתא: a tiny house is not divided between brothers or partners. It infers that a house of 4 by 4 אמות would be divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says brothers and partners do not divide it. The reason is that it is less than 4 אמות. That implies: if it has 4 אמות, they do divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא about the tiny house and draws an inference from it. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a tiny house cannot be split between heirs or partners. The גמרא reads it closely: the only reason given is that it is under 4 by 4 אמות. So a 4 by 4 house would be split.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers. Here it means heirs who inherited property together.
Partners who own property together.
They divide (the property between them).
The reason. The גמרא uses it to draw a close inference from the wording.
But then, by implication. It introduces the opposite case.

phrases.english: And brothers and partners do not divide it.
The reason is that it does not have four cubits;

phrases.aramaic: הָא אִית בֵּיהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת — חוֹלְקִין,
phrases.english: but if it has four cubits, they do divide it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the rules of the ברייתא about a tiny house, then draws an inference from this new line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tiny house is not divided between heirs or partners. By inference, a 4 by 4 house would be divided.

steps.title: A משנה requires 4 אמות for each partner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference from a משנה. A חצר is divided only if each partner would get 4 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: a courtyard is not divided unless there are 4 אמות for this one and 4 אמות for that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the inference from the last step by quoting a משנה. That משנה needs much more space before anything can be divided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference implied that a total of 4 by 4 אמות is enough to divide. The משנה says each partner must receive 4 אמות of his own, so the whole area must be at least twice as big. A 4 by 4 house should therefore still not be divided.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard shared by several houses.
For this one and for that one. It means each partner.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: one does not divide the courtyard

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לָזֶה
phrases.english: unless there will be in it four cubits for this one
and four cubits for that one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a house of 4 by 4 אמות is divided between partners.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires 4 אמות for each partner, so a total of only 4 by 4 is not enough to divide.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as being about the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes how the ברייתא is read. It does not mean the house itself is divided. It means the tiny house does not get the courtyard-division rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: the rule of dividing like a courtyard does not apply to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא is not talking about splitting the tiny house itself, so there is no clash with the משנה. Its point is that when the houses around a חצר divide the courtyard, a tiny house does not count toward a share.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say. It introduces a new way to read the text.
The law of dividing (property).

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the tiny house is now split into pieces. The new reading is about the shared courtyard outside it: the tiny house does not earn a share of that courtyard.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
The rule of division like a courtyard does not apply to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about splitting the tiny house itself between partners.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the tiny house gets no share when the courtyard is divided.

steps.title: How a courtyard is divided: by its doorways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two rulings on how a חצר is divided. רב הונא says by the number of doorways. רב חסדא says each doorway gets 4 אמות and the rest is split equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: a courtyard is divided according to its doorways. רב חסדא said: each doorway gets 4 אמות, and the rest is divided equally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the 'rule of dividing like a courtyard' is. It brings two אמוראים who show that houses earn courtyard space through their doorways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the whole courtyard is split by how many doorways open into it, so more doorways mean a bigger share. For רב חסדא, each doorway first gets 4 אמות in front of it, and the leftover is split evenly. Under both views, a house with a doorway affects the division, and this is what the tiny house will lose.

keyTerms.meaning: Its doorways, meaning the doors of the houses that open into the courtyard.
Is divided.
Equally.

phrases.english: As Rav Huna said:
A courtyard is divided according to its entrances.
And Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן לְכׇל פֶּתַח וָפֶתַח אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: One gives four cubits for each and every entrance,
and the rest they divide equally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the courtyard-division rule mentioned in the new reading of step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: a courtyard is divided by the number of doorways. רב חסדא: each doorway gets 4 אמות, and the rest is split equally.

steps.title: A house meant to be torn down gets no courtyard share
steps.stepSummary: These courtyard rules apply only to a house built to last. A tiny house is expected to be torn down, so it gets no share of the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: These rules apply to a house that is meant to stay standing, so we give it courtyard space. This tiny house is meant to be torn down, so we do not give it courtyard space.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation. It tells us why the tiny house is left out of the courtyard division.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doorway earns courtyard space only because a lasting house needs the courtyard for access and use. A house under 4 by 4 אמות is not fit to live in and will likely be torn down, so it is treated as if it were not there. This matches step 18: the tiny house is not suited to its purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply. It limits a rule to certain cases.
It stands to last, meaning it is built to stay.
It stands to be torn down.
We give.

steps.whatToRemember: A house smaller than 4 by 4 אמות is not treated as a real house. It earns no share of the courtyard, because the courtyard rules are only for houses meant to last.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the theme of this section: a structure under 4 by 4 אמות is not a real dwelling, and many laws ignore it.

phrases.english: For these words apply to a house that stands to endure:
we give it courtyard space.
This one, which stands to be torn down,
phrases.notes: This is the tiny house under 4 by 4 אמות, which nobody will keep living in.

phrases.english: we do not give it courtyard space.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rules of step 22 and explains why the tiny house is left out.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Courtyard space is given only to houses meant to last. A tiny house, which is expected to be torn down, gets none.

steps.title: Cushions and blankets do not lower a too-tall סוכה
steps.stepSummary: If a סוכה is higher than twenty אמות and someone tries to lower it by piling cushions and blankets on the floor, it does not count as a reduction, and the סוכה stays פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the סוכה was taller than twenty אמות, and a person tried to make it shorter by putting cushions and blankets on the floor, that is not considered making it shorter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule that a סוכה over twenty אמות is פסול. It teaches that raising the floor with cushions and blankets does not fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you can make a too-tall סוכה כשר by raising the floor so the space under the סכך is less than twenty אמות. Here the גמרא says that cushions and blankets do not count for this. They are not something a person leaves on the floor for good, so the floor has not really changed. This fits the idea in step 23, where something not meant to last did not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty cubits, the highest a סוכה may be
To make it smaller, here meaning to lower its height
Cushions and blankets (bedding)
A reduction, here a lowering of the סוכה's height that counts in הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a סוכה can never be lowered by raising the floor. It only says that cushions and blankets do not work for this.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that to fix a too-tall סוכה, what you put on the floor must really change the floor. Things that will soon be picked up do not count.

phrases.english: If [the סוכה] was higher than twenty cubits
and one came to reduce it
phrases.notes: He means lowering the height between the floor and the סכך by raising the floor.

phrases.english: with cushions and blankets
it is not a reduction

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה גְּבוֹהָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וּבָא לְמַעֲטָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the courtyard and tiny-house discussion and returns to the משנה's rule about a סוכה over twenty אמות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Placing cushions and blankets on the floor of a סוכה taller than twenty אמות does not count as lowering it, so the סוכה stays פסול.
